# XN-024 — GEOS execution ladder: do TreeSim gains show up when the decks actually run?

*Generated by research-copilot*

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Thread:** A2 of the NeurIPS 2026 author-response sprint (submission 31642)
**Status:** rungs 0–5 measured on 3 held-out tasks × 6 cells × 3 seeds (54 decks) + 4 reference decks
**Raw data:** `neurips_review/sprint/artifacts/A2_*` · **full method + command log:** `neurips_review/sprint/threads/A2_execution_rungs45.md`

## What this is (and is not)

The AC's primary objection is that the paper measures **structural** similarity (TreeSim) rather than
whether decks execute. This note answers the narrower, answerable question:

> On the held-out tasks where the paper's gain actually lives, do TreeSim differences correspond to
> differences in execution outcome and in simulated physics?

It is a **calibration study on 3 tasks**, not a physics benchmark. Every claim below is scoped to
that. Nothing here should be quoted as "SIGA produces better simulations" in general.

## Setup

- Binary: `/data/jixuan/.../install-your-platform-release/bin/geosx`, built **Jan 14 2026**, generated
  schema has **263 unique elements** vs 269 in the repo XSD (older strict subset). Requires
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- Ladder, all criteria fixed **before** looking at generated results, applied identically to reference
  and generated decks; **600 s wall-clock cap** everywhere:

  | rung | criterion |
  |---|---|
  | L0 | every XML in the deck set is well-formed |
  | L1 | top deck passes `xmllint --schema` |
  | L2 | `geosx -v -i` exits 0 |
  | L3 | full run exits 0 **and** the log contains `Cleaning up events` (time-stepping truly finished) |
  | L4 | L3 and zero timestep cuts, zero retried attempts, no Newton/line-search failures |
  | L4-ref-fidelity | L3 and the run reproduces the **reference's** timestep and retry counts |
  | L5 | relative error vs the reference run ≤ 10% on the task's primary scalar |

- **Task selection by rule** (top-2 TreeSim spread across cells, `TutorialHydraulicFractureWithAdvancedXML`
  excluded as a universal 0.013 failure, plus one ceiling control): returned
  `AdvancedExampleThermoPoroElasticWellbore` (0.355 → 0.761) and `ExampleProppantTest` (0.541 → 0.825),
  matching the pre-registered expectation, plus `AdvancedExampleViscoExtendedDruckerPrager` as the
  ceiling control (all cells 0.963–0.999).
- **Cell means use failures-as-zero**, per `XN-011`. Verified to 4 dp against Thread D's independent
  recompute for all six cells.

## NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST

**This study does not demonstrate an execution-level or physics-level advantage for SIGA over
Vanilla on these three tasks.** The large held-out TreeSim gap (ThermoPoro 0.355 → 0.761) does
**not** translate into a corresponding gap at rungs 2–5. Concretely, after fixing three bugs in my
own harness (see below), Vanilla reaches L2/L3/L4 on 2/3 seeds vs SIGA's 12/15 — indistinguishable
at n = 3.

**And the strongest single result is negative for TreeSim as a proxy.** On the ceiling-control task,
where every cell scores TreeSim **0.963–0.999**, **11 of 17 runs differ from the reference by
40–99%** on the primary QoI. Six reproduce it exactly. No cell is reliably better.

The verified cause is a blind spot in the metric: `triaxialDriver_base.xml` drives the test through
`TableFunction` data files (`tables/time.geos`, `axialStrain.geos`, `radialStress.geos`) that **the
agents author and TreeSim never reads** — it compares XML trees only. Diffed directly:

```
GT    : time = 0 1 2 3 4 5         axialStrain = 0.0 -0.004 -0.002 -0.005 -0.003 -0.006
F8_s2 : time = 0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1   axialStrain = 0.0 -0.003 -0.001 -0.004 -0.002      -> 99.3% error
F6_s3 : time = 0.0 0.1 ... 1.0     axialStrain halved throughout                      -> 71.0% error
SE_s2 : IDENTICAL to GT on all three                                                  ->  0.000% error
```
Both runs whose tables are byte-identical to GT give exactly 0% error. A deck scoring **0.999** on
TreeSim sat on top of a **99%** physics error.

This supports the AC's request rather than rebutting it: an execution check buys something a
structural metric cannot.

## What the study does establish

**1. Rungs 3–5 are reachable and cheap.** The binary works; a full ladder over 54 decks plus
reference runs is minutes-to-hours, not days. The smoke variant of ThermoPoro runs in ~8 s.

**2. GEOS is bitwise deterministic — verified, not assumed.** Two independent runs of the identical
reference deck agree on **all 16 statistics across 4 fields, to the last bit**. One execution per
deck suffices; the 3 seeds are *agent* seeds, never simulator repeats.

**3. Converged does not mean correct.** `F8_s1` on ThermoPoro is **L4-clean** (ran to final time,
zero timestep cuts, zero Newton retries) and yet **99.97% wrong**, on a 16-cell mesh instead of 40.

**4. Schema-valid does not mean loadable — and it fails in both directions.**
- `F4_s1` (DruckerPrager) declares `ElasticIsotropic` with **no elastic constants at all**. Every
  attribute is optional in the XSD, so it is schema-valid, and TreeSim scores it ≈0.99. GEOS refuses
  it: `numConstantsSpecified != 2`.
- Conversely, **GEOS parses with pugixml, which accepts `--` inside XML comments** where `xmllint`
  and ElementTree both reject it. So decks can fail well-formedness and still run. **The ladder is
  therefore not monotone** (L0/L1 use libxml2 semantics, L2+ use pugixml).

**5. Vanilla emits standards-illegal XML; SIGA does not.** 3 of 6 Vanilla case-study runs contain
`--` inside a comment, vs **0 of 23** SIGA runs. Because GEOS is lenient this is a **portability /
tooling defect** (it breaks `xmllint`, schema CI, and standard parsers) rather than an execution
failure. Stated that way it still stands.

**6. Where the reference itself does not converge, absolute L4 measures the wrong thing.**
`ExampleProppantTest`'s own reference deck needs 10 retried timesteps (reproducible). Under
absolute L4, SE scores 0/3; but SE's runs reproduce the reference's convergence signature
*exactly* (314 steps, 10 retries), while cells scoring "better" on absolute L4 *differ* from the
reference. Reference-fidelity is the informative criterion there, and on it SE leads 3/3.

**7. `ExampleMCCWellbore` is unusable.** Its reference deck hits the 600 s cap at t = 0.75 of
maxTime = 1.0, reproducibly. Excluded on reference-deck behaviour alone, before scoring any
generated MCC deck.

## Three bugs in my own harness — all found by Thread A1, all biased toward our own claim

1. **Deck copy dropped agent-authored non-XML assets.** I copied only `*.xml` and then overlaid GT's
   `tables/`, deleting files the agents wrote (`zeroStrain.geos`) and recording the result as deck
   failures. This also *masked finding #1 above* by forcing every run down the reference's loading
   path. Fixed; now copies the whole tree, GT fills only genuine gaps, with an assertion that the
   copy covers the source.
2. **L2 was cascaded from L0/L1 rather than measured.** Because GEOS is more permissive than
   `xmllint`, this under-reported what GEOS accepts — in the direction that flattered SIGA. Vanilla's
   ThermoPoro L2 was 1/3; measured unconditionally it is **2/3**. Fixed.
3. **My QoI injector was stricter than GEOS** (ElementTree rejected the `--` comments GEOS runs),
   inflating rung-5 failures for exactly the Vanilla decks at issue. Fixed with a lenient parse.

A separate contamination incident invalidated an earlier pass entirely: at 6-way concurrency on a
loaded box, valid runs were SIGKILLed and one reference deck was scored "L2 fail" that passes in 5 s
serially. Re-run with retry-on-signal. Discarded sets are retained as `.v1_*` / `.v2_*` for audit.

## Method notes that matter

- **QoI method: preference (a), identical injected observable.** The same
  `<VTK plotLevel="3">` + final-time `PeriodicEvent` is appended to reference and generated decks
  alike; scalars are then **mesh-independent reductions** (min/max/mean/L2) of the final state. No
  interpolation between different meshes is performed anywhere. `<VTK>` was chosen over
  `<TimeHistory>` precisely because it needs no region/field names and so cannot fail to attach
  merely because a deck renamed a region.
- **A contamination incident invalidated the first pass.** At 6-way concurrency on a loaded box,
  valid runs were SIGKILLed (`rc = -9`); one reference deck was scored "L2 fail" that passes in 5 s
  when run serially. All results were re-run with retry-on-signal and lower concurrency. The v1
  files are retained as `.v1_*_contaminated.jsonl` for audit and must not be used.
- **Disclosed normalizations:** GT's `tables/*.geos` data files are copied into every run directory
  (reference and generated identically) since authoring them was never part of the task; two DP
  failures (`F4_s2`, `F8_s1`) are caused by decks referencing a table filename GT does not provide,
  and are reported separately from genuine defects.

## Honest limitations

- **3 tasks, 3 seeds per cell. Underpowered by construction** — it cannot resolve the ~13-point
  differences at issue. Treat every cell-vs-cell comparison as directional at best.
- Not a physics benchmark. Do not generalize.
- `ExampleMCCWellbore` was deprioritized on cost after its reference deck needed ≥341 s; that
  decision was made from reference-deck behaviour only, before scoring any generated MCC deck.
- On ThermoPoro only three distinct relative errors occur (0.00%, 10.47%, 99.97%), and the declared
  10% tolerance falls *between* the first two clusters — so L5 pass/fail there is decided entirely by
  that gap. Robust readings: on exact reproduction SE leads 2/3 vs Vanilla 1/3; at ≤15% every cell is
  ≥2/3 and indistinguishable.
- Rung-5 numbers for `ExampleProppantTest` are **provisional** (carried from the pre-fix pass; the
  only relevant fix, the lenient injector, would only *add* Vanilla data points). Marked
  `qoi_provenance` in `A2_grid_qoi.jsonl`.
- The 10% L5 tolerance is arbitrary. Raw relative errors are in `A2_qoi_per_run.csv`.
- One binary, one machine, one build.
